282319169_32f8ec9e.text: Kisspeptin (Kiss1) neurons are crucial regulators of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis (HPG), making them essential for reproductive function. While primarily located in the hypothalamus where they control gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) secretion, additional Kiss1 neurons are found in areas outside of the hypothalamus, particularly in limbic areas, such as the lateral septum (LS). The LS, comprising ventral (VLS) and intermediate (ILS) divisions, integrates social, feeding, anxiety, and fear behaviors, and Kiss1 neurons in this region are regulated by sex steroids
282319169_32f8ec9e.section: Functional Roles in Reproductive Neuroendocrine Control

282319169_fd8ebee1.text: Quantitative analysis revealed a marked sexual dimorphism, with females showing significantly more Kiss1ILS compared to males (Male: 7.00 ± 2.864 vs. Female: 74.40 ± 17.68 neurons, **P = 0.0043). This sexual dimorphism was absent in Kiss1VLS neurons.
